content: The references provided are a collection of studies, reviews, and clinical trials focusing on various aspects of the treatment and management of drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB), including multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB). These studies explore the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of different therapeutic agents and regimens, as well as adjunctive therapies and supportive care strategies. 1. Linezolid-Induced Lactic Acidosis: Studies by Kwon HY et al. and Mao Y et al. investigate the incidence and risk factors associated with lactic acidosis caused by linezolid, a key drug in treating drug-resistant TB. These studies highlight the importance of monitoring for metabolic complications during treatment. 2. Linezolid for Drug-Resistant TB: Research by Lee M et al. and others demonstrates the effectiveness of linezolid in treating chronic extensively drug-resistant TB, emphasizing its bactericidal activity and safety profile. 3. Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics in TB Treatment: Technical reports and studies, such as those by the WHO, provide insights into the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of drugs used in drug-resistant TB treatment, aiding in optimizing dosing strategies. 4. Short-Course Regimens for MDR-TB: Studies by Kuaban C et al. and Trébucq A et al. evaluate the effectiveness of short-course regimens for MDR-TB in various settings, including African countries, showing promising outcomes in terms of treatment success and relapse prevention. 5. Surgical Interventions in MDR-TB: Research by Fox GJ et al. and Kang MW et al. explores the role of surgery as an adjunctive treatment for MDR-TB, particularly in cases with localized disease or extensive drug resistance. 6. Combination Therapies with Bedaquiline and Delamanid: Studies by Maryandyshev A et al. and Ferlazzo G et al. assess the safety and efficacy of combining bedaquiline and delamanid for treating XDR-TB, providing evidence for their use in challenging cases. 7. Adjunctive Corticosteroid Therapy: Multiple studies, including those by Schoeman JF et al. and Thwaites GE et al., investigate the use of corticosteroids like dexamethasone in managing TB meningitis and pericarditis, showing benefits in reducing inflammation and improving outcomes. 8. Interferon-Gamma as Adjunctive Therapy: Research by Koh WJ et al. and Suarez-Mendez R et al. evaluates the use of interferon-gamma in refractory MDR-TB cases, with mixed results regarding its therapeutic role. 9. Adherence and Decentralized Care: Studies by Alipanah N et al. and Ho J et al. highlight the importance of adherence interventions and decentralized care models in improving treatment outcomes for MDR-TB patients. 10. Patient Support and Comprehensive Care: Reports and reviews, such as those by Cocozza A et al. and Campbell J et al., emphasize the need for comprehensive supportive care, including psychosocial and nutritional support, to enhance treatment success in drug-resistant TB. 11. High-Dose Isoniazid and Other Novel Approaches: Trials like those by Katiyar SK et al. explore the use of high-dose isoniazid and other innovative therapies to improve outcomes in MDR-TB treatment. 12. Maternal and Infant Outcomes in TB: Studies by Loveday M et al. examine the impact of MDR-TB treatment on pregnant women and their infants, providing critical data on safety and outcomes in this vulnerable population. 13. Global and Regional TB Management Strategies: References to WHO operational handbooks and other guidelines underscore the global efforts to standardize and improve the management of drug-resistant TB through evidence-based practices. These references collectively provide a comprehensive overview of the advancements, challenges, and ongoing research in the field of drug-resistant TB treatment, offering valuable insights for clinicians and researchers.
